syllabus_extract: Lift augmentation. High lift devices. Boundary Layer control
specific_objectives: 6.1.2.1 Trainee will be able to describe various types of aerofoil sections, conditions of performance, theories, and concept related with performance

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of IB diagrams regarding flap deflection angles and boundary layer separation points; Instructor supervision of diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of high lift devices?
How does increasing the angle of attack affect the lift coefficient?
Define the boundary layer in the context of wing performance.

development.content:
Types of High Lift Devices
Slats and Leading Edge Flaps
Trailing Edge Flaps
Flap Deflection Angles

Boundary Layer Control Methods
Vortex Generators Function
Blowing and Suction Systems
Boundary Layer Transition

Performance Impact of Augmentation
Stall Speed Reduction
Takeoff and Landing Efficiency
Drag Penalty Considerations

summary_questions: Explain how a leading edge slat delays flow separation.
Describe the trade-off between lift augmentation and drag increase.
Identify two methods used for active boundary layer control.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the operational advantages of slats versus trailing edge flaps for takeoff and landing phases, referencing LP 16 concepts on control surface limitations.
